subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the 300Tdi across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The 300Tdi is a single-application engine, fitted exclusively to the Defender (L316) from 1994 to 1998.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing belt and tensioner, main bearings, connecting rod bearings, head gasket, complete gasket and seal set, oil filter housing gasket.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The 300Tdi is an interference engine — timing belt failure causes piston-to-valve contact. Turbocharger bearing failure and VE fuel injection pump leaks are also known issues on higher-mileage examples. Head gasket failure is common.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed 300Tdi rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: LAND ROVER 300Tdi REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: A full 300Tdi rebuild involves stripping the 2.5L (2,495 cc) Inline-4 (I4) diesel engine down, inspecting the crankshaft, cylinder head and VE injection pump, and replacing the timing belt, bearings, gaskets and seals with updated OEM-specification parts.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing Belt, Main Bearings and Connecting Rod Bearings, Complete Gasket and Seal Set, Oil Filter Housing Gasket
